12	# The Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
13	
14	This file states Milne's
15	*Abelian Varieties* §III.6 Proposition 6.1: for a complete nonsingular curve
16	`C` of genus `g > 0` over an algebraically closed field `k̄` and a marked
17	`k̄`-point `P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`, the Abel–Jacobi morphism
18	`ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is the **Albanese morphism** of the pointed curve
19	`(C, P₀)`: any pointed morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety with
20	`φ(P₀) = η_A` factors uniquely as `φ = ψ ∘ ι_{P₀}` for a homomorphism of
21	group schemes `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`.
22	
23	The route taken is the **symmetric-power route** (cube-free): the
24	symmetric assignment `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` factors through
25	`Sym^g C`, the resulting morphism `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` descends through
26	the birational morphism `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` to a rational map
27	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`, and Milne's Theorem I.3.2 (`extend_to_av` in the sibling
28	`Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`, A.4.c) promotes it to a regular
29	morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`. The group-homomorphism property of `ψ` then
30	follows from `ψ(η_J) = η_A` together with Milne Corollary I.1.2 (a
31	consequence of `thm:rigidity_lemma`).
32	
33	## Main results
34	
35	* `Pic0.abelJacobi` — the regular morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
36	  (`lem:abel_jacobi_morphism`).
37	* `Pic0.SymmetricPower` — the `g`-th symmetric power `Sym^g C` of the curve
38	  `C`, as a `k̄`-scheme (Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1).
39	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerAVMap` — the symmetrised morphism
40	  `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` induced by a morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian
41	  variety.
42	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the birational morphism
43	  `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`.
44	* `Pic0.descentThroughBirationalSigma` — the descent of `Sym^g φ` to a unique
45	  regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`, via Milne Theorem I.3.2.
46	* `Pic0.albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — the connecting biconditional:
47	  `φ = ι_{P₀} ≫ ψ` holds iff `Sym^g φ = f^{(g)} ≫ ψ`.
48	* `Pic0.albanese_universal_property` — the universal property itself (Milne
49	  Proposition III.6.1), assembled from the previous two.
50	
51	## Remaining obligations
52	
53	`albanese_universal_property` is assembled from
54	`descentThroughBirationalSigma` and `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq`, but
55	six declarations of this file are stated without proof:
56	
57	* `abelJacobi` — the moduli classifier of the rigidified diagonal
58	  correspondence `𝓛^{P₀} = 𝓞_{C × C}(Δ − {P₀} × C − C × {P₀})`, taken as a
59	  relative degree-zero line bundle over the second factor.
60	* `SymmetricPower` — the affine-and-glue construction `Spec(A^{⊗ g})^{S_g}`
61	  of Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 (Mumford 1970 §II.7 / §III.11). Mathlib has
62	  no scheme-theoretic symmetric power, only `Sym` for types and modules.
63	* `symmetricPowerAVMap` and `symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the two invocations
64	  of the universal property of `Sym^g C`, which need the symmetric projection
65	  `π : C^g ⟶ Sym^g C` supplied by that construction.
66	* `descentThroughBirationalSigma` — extension of the rational map
67	  `Sym^g φ ∘ (f^{(g)})^{-1}` to a regular morphism (Milne Theorem I.3.2).
68	* `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — Milne's identification of `ι_{P₀}`
69	  with `Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` followed by `f^{(g)}`.
70	
71	## The scheme `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
72	
73	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is taken from `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` through a thin
74	`Pic0.Bundle` structure that carries the underlying scheme together with its
75	four abelian-variety attributes (`GrpObj`, `IsProper`, `Smooth`,
76	`GeometricallyIrreducible`), the carrier `Pic0.bundle C`, and the derived
77	definition `Pic0.jacobianScheme C := (bundle C).scheme`.
78	
79	The upstream declarations `Scheme.Pic0.{grpObj, proper, smooth,
80	geometricallyIrreducible}` run under `[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]`,
81	`[HasPicScheme C]` and `[PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]`, whereas
82	the Albanese curve enters carrying only smoothness, properness and geometric
83	irreducibility over `k̄`. The three bridges of §0.0
84	(`geometricallyReduced_of_smooth`, `GeometricallyIntegral.of_…`,
85	`hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed`) discharge the missing hypotheses over an
86	algebraically closed base.
87	
88	## Abelian-variety conventions
89	
90	Following the project (cf. `AbelianVarietyRigidity.lean`, `Jacobian.lean`),
91	an **abelian variety over `k̄`** is encoded as an object
92	`A : Over (Spec (.of k̄))` carrying the four instances:
93	
94	- `[GrpObj A]` (group-object structure on the over-category),
95	- `[IsProper A.hom]` (complete),
96	- `[Smooth A.hom]` (nonsingular),
97	- `[GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]` (geometrically irreducible).
98	
99	A **smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over `k̄`** carries:
100	
101	- `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]`,
102	- `[IsProper C.hom]`,
103	- `[GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]`.
104	
105	These instances are supplied by `inferInstance` at the call site.
106

551	For a complete nonsingular curve `C` of genus `g > 0` over an
552	algebraically closed field `k̄`, a marked `k̄`-point `P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`, and
553	every pointed morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety `A` with

557	Proof sketch (Milne III.6.1):
558	1. **Symmetrisation.** `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` is
559	   `S_g`-symmetric (`A` commutative), so factors through
560	   `Sym^g C` as `Sym^g φ` (`lem:symmetric_product_av_map`).
561	2. **Descent to a regular morphism on `J`.** The birational morphism
562	   `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` (`lem:symmetric_product_to_jacobian`)
563	   exhibits `Sym^g φ ∘ (f^{(g)})^{-1}` as a rational map
564	   `Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`, which by Milne Theorem I.3.2 extends uniquely to
565	   a regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`
566	   (`lem:descent_through_birational_sigma`).
567	3. **Factorisation `ψ ∘ ι_{P₀} = φ`.** Use Milne's identification of
568	   `ι_{P₀}` with the composite `Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` followed by
569	   `f^{(g)}`; together with `φ(P₀) = η_A` and the additive structure
570	   of `A`, this gives `ψ(ι_{P₀}(Q)) = φ(Q)` on `k̄`-points, hence
571	   globally by the reduced-and-separated agreement principle.
572	4. **Homomorphism property.** `ψ` sends `η_J = ι_{P₀}(P₀)` to
573	   `φ(P₀) = η_A`, so by Milne Corollary I.1.2 (a `thm:rigidity_lemma`
574	   consequence) it is a homomorphism of group schemes.
575	5. **Uniqueness.** Two homomorphisms `Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` with the same
576	   restriction to `ι_{P₀}(C)` agree on the `g`-fold sum
577	   `ι_{P₀}(C) + ⋯ + ι_{P₀}(C) = Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` (since `f^{(g)}` is
578	   surjective), hence are equal.
579

24	symmetric assignment `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` factors through
25	`Sym^g C`, the resulting morphism `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` descends through
26	the birational morphism `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` to a rational map
27	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`, and Milne's Theorem I.3.2 (`extend_to_av` in the sibling
28	`Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`, A.4.c) promotes it to a regular
29	morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`. The group-homomorphism property of `ψ` then
30	follows from `ψ(η_J) = η_A` together with Milne Corollary I.1.2 (a
31	consequence of `thm:rigidity_lemma`).
32	
33	## Main results
34	
35	* `Pic0.abelJacobi` — the regular morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
36	  (`lem:abel_jacobi_morphism`).
37	* `Pic0.SymmetricPower` — the `g`-th symmetric power `Sym^g C` of the curve
38	  `C`, as a `k̄`-scheme (Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1).
39	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerAVMap` — the symmetrised morphism
40	  `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` induced by a morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian
41	  variety.
42	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the birational morphism
43	  `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`.
44	* `Pic0.descentThroughBirationalSigma` — the descent of `Sym^g φ` to a unique
45	  regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`, via Milne Theorem I.3.2.
46	* `Pic0.albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — the connecting biconditional:
47	  `φ = ι_{P₀} ≫ ψ` holds iff `Sym^g φ = f^{(g)} ≫ ψ`.
48	* `Pic0.albanese_universal_property` — the universal property itself (Milne
49	  Proposition III.6.1), assembled from the previous two.
50	
51	## Remaining obligations
52	
53	`albanese_universal_property` is assembled from
54	`descentThroughBirationalSigma` and `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq`, but
55	six declarations of this file are stated without proof:
56	
57	* `abelJacobi` — the moduli classifier of the rigidified diagonal
58	  correspondence `𝓛^{P₀} = 𝓞_{C × C}(Δ − {P₀} × C − C × {P₀})`, taken as a
59	  relative degree-zero line bundle over the second factor.
60	* `SymmetricPower` — the affine-and-glue construction `Spec(A^{⊗ g})^{S_g}`
61	  of Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 (Mumford 1970 §II.7 / §III.11). Mathlib has
62	  no scheme-theoretic symmetric power, only `Sym` for types and modules.
63	* `symmetricPowerAVMap` and `symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the two invocations
64	  of the universal property of `Sym^g C`, which need the symmetric projection
65	  `π : C^g ⟶ Sym^g C` supplied by that construction.
66	* `descentThroughBirationalSigma` — extension of the rational map
67	  `Sym^g φ ∘ (f^{(g)})^{-1}` to a regular morphism (Milne Theorem I.3.2).
68	* `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — Milne's identification of `ι_{P₀}`
69	  with `Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` followed by `f^{(g)}`.

71	## The scheme `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
72	
73	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is taken from `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` through a thin
74	`Pic0.Bundle` structure that carries the underlying scheme together with its
75	four abelian-variety attributes (`GrpObj`, `IsProper`, `Smooth`,
76	`GeometricallyIrreducible`), the carrier `Pic0.bundle C`, and the derived
77	definition `Pic0.jacobianScheme C := (bundle C).scheme`.

88	## Abelian-variety conventions
89	
90	Following the project (cf. `AbelianVarietyRigidity.lean`, `Jacobian.lean`),
91	an **abelian variety over `k̄`** is encoded as an object
92	`A : Over (Spec (.of k̄))` carrying the four instances:

/-- **Inverse of an invertible module.**

Every line bundle `L : X.Modules` has a two-sided tensor inverse: its sheaf dual

`homOfLocalCompat` glues the local maps, while `isIso_of_isIso_restrict` promotes their

    (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L) :
    ∃ Linv : X.Modules, LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial Linv ∧

  by
  classical
  -- `Linv := dual L`; locally trivial by the **C-bridge** `dual_isLocallyTrivial`.
  refine ⟨dual L, dual_isLocallyTrivial hL, ?_⟩
  -- Choose, for each point, a trivialising affine open of `L` together with the
  -- trivialisation `eM x : L|_{U x} ≅ 𝒪_{U x}`.
